root_cause: CachingTest.LoadMultiWithConfig_race spawns multiple concurrent threads that race to load/import the same cached model via a mock plugin, and asserts an exact EXPECT_CALL count (6) on mock_plugin->import_model(). The test's own log line ('Caching LoadMulti Test completed. Tried 115 times') shows it internally retries the race until a target condition is met, but the retry loop does not guarantee the mocked import_model() is invoked exactly 6 times under Windows CI timing/scheduling variance - on this run only 5 calls were observed before the loop's termination condition was satisfied, leaving one EXPECT_CALL unsatisfied. This is a pre-existing timing-sensitive test design issue in src/inference/tests/functional/caching_test.cpp and is unrelated to the triggering commit (#38851), which only changes MLIR header include style in the GPU plugin and does not touch caching/import_model code.
reproduction_steps: Not reliably reproducible outside CI; requires Windows scheduling conditions. Locally: build with -DENABLE_TESTS=ON, run `ov_inference_functional_tests --gtest_filter=CachingTest/CachingTest.LoadMultiWithConfig_race*` repeatedly (hundreds of iterations) on a loaded Windows machine to attempt to trigger the race; failure rate is low and timing-dependent.
recommended_actions: Relax the exact EXPECT_CALL(*mockPlugin, import_model(...)).Times(6) expectation in caching_test.cpp around line 2670 to an AtLeast()/range-based expectation, or make the race-loop (the one producing 'Caching LoadMulti Test completed. Tried N times') guarantee the exact call count deterministically before asserting.
Add a short synchronization barrier/wait after the racing threads join and before Mock::VerifyAndClearExpectations so late-arriving import_model() calls are captured.
Consider marking LoadMultiWithConfig_race (and the sibling LoadMulti_race tests) as known-flaky on Windows with a retry/quarantine mechanism if the above fix is not quick to land.

If this recurs frequently, file/update a tracking issue referencing src/inference/tests/functional/caching_test.cpp:2670 and :315 so maintainers of the caching test suite can adjust the race test design.
prevention_strategies: Avoid asserting exact gmock call counts in tests that deliberately introduce concurrency races; prefer bounded ranges (e.g., Between(min,max) or AtLeast) when the number of calls depends on thread scheduling. Add explicit synchronization (e.g., a latch/barrier) before verifying mock expectations in multi-threaded cache-race tests.
historical_context: No prior CI Doctor Post-Commit investigation matches this exact signature (caching_test.cpp mock import_model count mismatch in LoadMultiWithConfig_race); this is the first recorded occurrence. Other Windows C++ unit test flakiness has been seen previously but under different signatures/patterns.
